reviewContext.userProblem: A Work Runtime task attempt that stalls because it needs the user (an answer, or the user's presence on a host) or because its owner died cannot be moved to another worker; the work is stuck on the original process and host.
requiredOutcomes: A task attempt that emits the handover envelope ends suspended, seals a packet with a stable digest, and task show lists it.
task answer + task takeover (same store) continues at the resume step with the answer in the step input and the history imported.
A repository task publishes riela/task/<id>/g<n> at handover; a takeover on a second clone materializes it and continues.
An attempt whose owner is killed is taken over with --force-orphan after lease expiry; the killed owner, if revived, fails with leaseLost.
A presence handover is refused on a host without the userReachable trait and accepted on one with it.
Remote takeover over /graphql heartbeats and reports; the controller runs verification and director on the reported outcome.
kaiba, gitRef, file and command sinks round-trip the packet with digest verification.

designDecisionsAndRationale: The task is the unit of handover: a handover is a new Attempt with entry .takeover, reusing the one-live-attempt fence, evidence ledger, placement and guard budget (design §3.1).
The digest-sealed HandoverPacket is the predecessor/successor contract, built by the runtime from durable records; the agent only adds a bounded progressNote and question (§3.2).
suspended is a real session status with a SuspendRecord; runner/resume exit code CLIExitCode.suspended = 5 (§3.3, R1-R22).
Agent-declared, runtime-detected and operator triggers all produce Decision .handover(HandoverReason) and the same packet (§3.4).
Deliverables are published before sealing: attempt branch riela/task/<taskId>/g<n> via GitBranchWorkspaceRuntime, document ids via DeliverableCollector, local-only state listed (§3.5, §9).
The work store work_handovers row is canonical; kaiba/gitRef/file/command sinks are digest-verified mirrors (§3.6, §8).
Answers are DecisionKind.answer validated against answerSchema and delivered as runtime variable plus delivered message (§3.7).
Hosts declare traits (profile hostTraits, worker.json traits, per-invocation --traits per Q7); placement treats required traits like backends (§3.8, §10.3).
Leases gain heartbeat_at, expires_at and a monotonic fence; the fence, not expiry, excludes a revived owner which fails with leaseLost (§3.9, §11).
Cross-host takeover is pull-based over /graphql (takeoverTask, heartbeatAttempt, reportAttempt) under manager-session auth; the controller runs director and verification on reports (§3.10, §10.2).
Host traits are [HostTrait] deduplicated and sorted at init with strict decode; placement compares them as sets (§21 R23).

DistributedWorkerStatus gains strict traits filled from the stored registration in DistributedJobController.workerStatuses, so workers()/inspectWorkers() expose declared worker traits; doctor shows local host traits only; placement still reads HostCapabilitySnapshot (§21 R24, observability only).

An answer binds to a handover only by task, predecessor attempt, handover id in the reason, question id and work_decisions.created_at >= work_handovers.created_at; WorkStore.latestAnswer(handoverId:) is the only lookup (§21 R25).

A triggered task attempt has exactly one terminal session write: the runner writes failed(<trigger kind>) through DeterministicWorkflowRunRequest.cancellationCause, validateTaskTerminalWrite accepts failed(.stalled) for a pending .handover cancellation, sealHandoverIfNeeded reloads and never re-saves, and a fenced owner (leaseLost) seals no packet (§21 R26).

Adoption claims the checkout: preflight before any row, git switch -c <riela/task branch> at HEAD carrying the dirty tree, isolation recorded on the terminal adopted attempt, sealed as a live owner without a lease fence so the branch is published (§21 R27).

Takeover handles the repository deliverable by state: .published and .unpublished materialize, .checkpointFailed is refused before any reservation and the task stays waiting (§21 R28, user-qa Q9 default).
intentionalTradeoffs: Mid-node interruption (S3, --now) re-runs the step; step-boundary checkpoints bound repository loss to one step.
The wait-signal classifier uses typed ACP tool-call status only, never free text; unclassified events fall back to inactivity.
The schema generation bump discards existing session stores.
A repository without a remote can only be handed over on the same host; --endpoint takeover of such a task is refused.
The wh-17 orphan example uses a never-launched owner; the running-owner leaseLost leg is proven by wh-14 TaskHandoverLeaseTests.
Parity/SDL gates stay red between wh-01 and wh-20; wh-20 owns catalog rows, SDL and the serial join audit.
supportedEdgeCases: Answer (S1), presence (S2), inactivity (S3 via handoverOnInactivity), operator (S4) and orphan (--force-orphan after lease expiry) handovers.
History import from suspended or failed(stalled|cancelled|leaseLost) same-store sessions and from packet bundles; truncated bundles refused.
Presence takeover refused without required traits (waiting host-traits-unavailable) and accepted with them.
Revived owner heartbeat returns fenced and the predecessor is reconciled failed/leaseLost.
Sink tamper detection via kind:locator#sha256 digest verification.
riela gc removes handover files/refs of terminal or absent tasks, keeps non-terminal ones, fails closed on a missing or locked database.
outOfScopeEdgeCases: Moving cwd-local riela memory or KV into packets (listed as local-only only).
Probing host traits (traits are declared, never probed).
